tpm_manager: rewrite context connection logic for TPM1.2 The current implementation is not accurate and has many defects: 1. error handling for communication failure doesn't consider the error layer. 2. 1 excessive 100ms sleep upon consistent communication failure. 3. when consistent communication failure, the logic falls the nullified checking, which gives a confusing message "Enexpected NULL context.", while it should be logging communication failure. 4. over-complicated loop for the retry loigc and unnecessarily deep nested loop. 5. context doesn't get reset after failed communication, which means the user could get an disconnected context for the second call of |GetContext|. bluetooth: Export GATT attribute interfaces as GATT client role In order to make the GATT attributes visible to D-Bus clients, this includes the following changes. - Adding gatt_interface_handler to export the discovered GATT services characteristics and descriptor to D-Bus - Implementation of observer mechanism in gatt.cc so that gatt_interface_handler can get notified on changes on GATT attributes - Determining how the D-Bus object properties should be updated and exported. We decided to go for the module where the interface handler needs to proactively go through all properties and update them. iproute2: Resync ARL qdisc attributes The ARL qdisc defines several Netlink attributes that are 64bit quantities. With the introduction of the nla_put_u64_64bit() helper [commit 73520786b079 ("libnl: add nla_put_u64_64bit() helper")] these attributes are forced to 64bit alignment. A new ARL attribute (TCA_ARL_PAD) is defined in the kernel pkt_sched.h file, which is inserted in the Netlink message when padding is required to achieve the necessary 64bit attribute alignment. The iproute2 package maintains its own private copy of the kernel pkt_sched.h file. This CL synchronizes the kernel TCA_ARL_xxx attribute list with the iproute2 private pkt_sched.h, this picks up the new TCA_ARL_PAD to ensure the 'tc qdisc show' command can properly recognize and decode Netlink messages when ARL Qdisc is active. FROMLIST: bluetooth: xbox controller bug fix The current L2CAP implementation does not change any options if the other side respons with "unknown options", but does if "unaccepted options" is the answer. It is up to the implementation to decide on the effort spent on config negotiations, therefore the current implementation is correct at this point - but many devices (like Xbox One S controllers) are not useable this way. A workaround for many users therefore is to disable_ertm, since this is often the option which is unknown. I would prefer to try it again with altered options instead of globally disable ERTM. In result, I suggest the following patch. It simply adds a new case (L2CAP_CONF_UNKNOWN), which does nothing but falling through to L2CAP_CONF_UNACCEPT. biod: bio_crypto_init stall boot It is possible for bio_crypto_init to still be running when boot-update-firmware is started. This is not good because both tasks interact with the fingerprint MCU in different incompatible ways. This change makes bio_crypto_init an upstart "task". This allows bio_crypto_init to stall the boot at the boot-services step, until bio_crypto_init has fully finished. This has the effect of delaying boot-update-firmware until bio_crypto_init has finished. Additionally, this ensures that fewer system processes are running while the seed is being set. The boot time implications have been analyzed in the following speadsheet: http://sheets/1O3QYv4KNZeqm-o_0_HQc9Z7BcP-FsAN_Gs9f9mk5jyc#gid=274630119 The discussion of the boot time implications are in the following bugs: BUG=b:130677245, b:119206742, chromium:992487 TEST=emerge-nocturne biod && cros deploy dut1 biod reboot TEST=emerge-nocturne biod && cros deploy dut1 biod ssh dut1 touch /var/log/biofw # Add the following to the top of the main script # section of/etc/init/bio_crypto_init.conf sleep 30 # Add the following to the end of the post-start # section of /etc/init/bio_crypto_init.conf rm /var/log/biofw # Add the following to top of the pre-start section # of /etc/init/boot-update-firmware.conf if [ -e /var/log/biofw ]; then logger -t "${UPSTART_JOB}" "bio_crypto_init is still running" else logger -t "${UPSTART_JOB}" "bio_crypto_init is NOT still running" fi # Now clear the logs and reboot rm -rf /var/log/* reboot grep --text bio_crypto_init /var/log/messages # Check that you see "bio_crypto_init is NOT still running" TEST=# Fetch nocturne device emerge-nocturne biod && cros deploy dut1 biod gsutil cat gs://chromeos-binaries/HOME/bcs-nocturne-private/overlay-nocturne-private/chromeos-base/chromeos-firmware-fpmcu-nocturne/nocturne_fp-2.2.67.tbz2 | tar xjv -C /tmp ssh dut1 mount -oremount,rw / scp /tmp/nocturne_fp_*.bin dut1:~/ ssh dut1 'flashrom --fast-verify --programmer=ec:type=fp --image=EC_RW --write ~/nocturne_fp_*.bin' ssh dut1 cat /dev/cros_fp ssh dut1 rm -rf '/var/log/*' ssh dut1 reboot ssh dut1 cat '/var/log/bio_crypto_init/bio_crypto_init.*' '/var/log/biod/bio_fw_updater.*' # Check that there are no errors Change-Id: Ieba22bde6263f373949e1f743eb0e6f5c78ffccf Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1725576 Tested-by: Craig Hesling <hesling@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Nicolas Norvez <norvez@chromium.org>

dlcservice: Change install logic acceptance The |Install()| of DLC(s) must gracefully handle scenrios. When an |Install()| is called: - Empty DLC list NOT allowed. - Unsupported DLC in list NOT allowed. - Duplicate DLC in list NOT allowed. - Already installed DLC allowed. It is now valid to pass in an already installed DLC(s), so there can be cases for install passed in as a high level view: Q1) Only already installed DLC(s). Q2) Already installed DLC(s) + unsupported DLC(s). Q3) Already installed DLC(s) + supported DLC(s). Q4) Already installed DLC(s) + supported DLC(s) + not supported DLC(s). |InstallResult| sent out is consistent and simple throughout the process: A1) Within |Install()| the call to send out |InstallResult| will include all the root mount points. A2) No |InstallResult| is sent out as this |Install()| call itself will fail. A3) On success, within |StatusUpdateAdvancedSignal()| the |InstallResult| sent out should include all the root mount points. On failure to allocate space during |Install()| there will be no |InstallResult| sent out as this |Install()| call itself will fail. On failure to mount or |ImageLoader| failure, |InstallResult| will include the root mount points of the previously installed and mounted DLC(s), but the newly installed DLC(s) will all be deleted with there root mount points set to an empty string. |InstallResult|'s success will be false and the corresponding error code will be set. A4) No |InstallResult| is sent out as this |Install()| call itself will fail. mount-encrypted: add the new cmdline option "insecure" mount-encrypted doesn't store an insecure system key in NVRAM, which allows us to keep encstateful not wiped over TPM clearing and avoids potential unexpected behavior caused by soft-clearing TPM 2.0. The option should only be enabled for testing purposes and will be used in the autotest env. This CL provdes an alternative and simpler way to solve the soft-clearing TPM 2.0 problem mentioned above, compared with the original solution in CL:1753389. BUG=b:139399088 TEST=tested along with CL:1763468: On a chell, make sure the changes are no-op in any case. On a soraka, create the magic file in /mnt/stateful_partition, then 1. Run crossystem to clear the TPM, reboot, and log in. Then, repeat those 3 steps a few times and make sure each time the encrypted partition is not wiped. Also, check if mount-encrypted.log says it uses an insecure system key. 2. Run tpm_softclear to soft-clear the TPM, then run tpm_manager_client take_ownership to re-own the TPM, then reboot. Make sure the encrypted partition isn't wiped and mount-encrypted.log says it uses an insecure system key. 3. Remove the magic file, run crossystem to clear the TPM, reboot, and make sure the encrypted partition is wiped and mount-encrypted.log says it creates a random key and stores it in NVRAM.
